Package io.micronaut.context.reload

@NullMarked package io.micronaut.context.reload
The contract between a development launcher that reloads the application's classes and the components that cache or register state derived from those classes.
Since:
5.3.0
Author:
graemerocher
  • Related Packages
    Package
    Description
    io.micronaut.context
    This package contains the core classes for starting a BeanContext.
  • Class
    Description
    AnnotatedBeanRetentionPolicy
    Retains the singletons whose definition is annotated with Retain: on the bean's class, or on the factory method that produces it.
    BeanRetentionPolicy
    Decides which singletons survive a restart of the application context: they are not destroyed with the old context and are adopted by the new one.
    BeanRetentionPolicy.Decision
    What a policy decides for a singleton.
    ClassChange
    One class the application changed.
    ClassChange.Kind
    The kind of change.
    ClassChangeEvent
    The application's classes changed: a development launcher compiled them into a new generation of the application classloader and is about to replace the beans of the retired generation.
    InPlaceResourceReloader
    Applies a change of the application's resources to the running application in place, so that a development launcher need not restart it.
    InPlaceResourceReloader.Result
    What a reload applied.
    PolicyRetentionCriteria
    What a restart retains according to BeanRetentionPolicy beans: a singleton a policy retains, unless a change touched a configuration prefix one of the policies that retain it declares for it, and unless a policy refuses it, whatever their order.
    ReloadCompletedEvent
    The new generation of the application's classes is in place: its bean definitions are registered and the context that now runs the application started its eager beans.
    ReloadStrategy
    How a development launcher applies a change of the application's classes.
    ResourceKind
    The kinds of resource roots a development launcher distinguishes, and a resource watch selects by.
    RetainingBeanContext
    A context that can stop retaining some of its singletons for the next one, so that what its stop shuts down, such as the graceful shutdown that the ShutdownEvent starts, leaves those running.
    RetentionCriteria
    What DefaultBeanContext.stopRetaining(RetentionCriteria) asks about the singletons of the context it stops, for a development launcher restarting the application: the combined answer of the BeanRetentionPolicy beans, which PolicyRetentionCriteria gives, and of what the launcher knows about the restart.
